scenarioStory.history: Bystanders report the patient was struck multiple times in the head and face during an altercation outside a bar, with a brief loss of consciousness. He regained some responsiveness, vomited twice, and has become progressively less responsive and unable to protect his airway since police arrived.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 28-year-old male supine outside a bar with visible head trauma, decreased level of consciousness, and blood-tinged emesis in the oropharynx. He is moaning and withdrawing to pain but not following commands or protecting his airway. → Preoxygenated for RSI: Crew suctions the airway, applies high-flow oxygen via non-rebreather, maintains cervical spine stabilization, and preoxygenates with positive pressure ventilation for at least two minutes while confirming blood pressure is adequate before proceeding to drug-assisted intubation. → RSI performed, tube confirmed: Crew administers fentanyl premedication, etomidate for induction, and rocuronium for paralysis, then successfully intubates and confirms tube placement with waveform capnography and bilateral breath sounds. → Ventilation controlled, transport: Tube is secured, sedation is maintained, ventilation rate is controlled to keep EtCO2 in the target range, and the patient is transported to a trauma center capable of managing severe TBI.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Decreased level of consciousness after assault

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 28-year-old male supine outside a bar with visible head trauma, decreased level of consciousness, and blood-tinged emesis in the oropharynx. He is moaning and withdrawing to pain but not following commands or protecting his airway.
relatedChecklist: Apply high-flow O2 via NRB; suction blood/emesis from oropharynx
Maintain cervical spine stabilization; assume concomitant C-spine injury
Reassess BP before sedative/paralytic; treat to maintain SBP ≥110 mmHg
Preoxygenate with high-flow O2 + PPV for at least 2 minutes before RSI attempt

scenarioEvents.name: Preoxygenated for RSI
scenarioEvents.description: Crew suctions the airway, applies high-flow oxygen via non-rebreather, maintains cervical spine stabilization, and preoxygenates with positive pressure ventilation for at least two minutes while confirming blood pressure is adequate before proceeding to drug-assisted intubation.
relatedChecklist: Fentanyl 85 mcg IV premedication (85 kg × 1 mcg/kg), 2–3 min prior to intubation
Etomidate 25 mg IV push induction (85 kg × 0.3 mg/kg = 25.5 mg)
Rocuronium 85 mg IV push paralytic (85 kg × 1 mg/kg)
Intubate; confirm placement with waveform capnography and bilateral breath sounds

scenarioEvents.name: RSI performed, tube confirmed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew administers fentanyl premedication, etomidate for induction, and rocuronium for paralysis, then successfully intubates and confirms tube placement with waveform capnography and bilateral breath sounds.
relatedChecklist: Ventilate at 10 breaths/min; target EtCO2 35–45 mmHg, avoid hyperventilation

scenarioEvents.name: Ventilation controlled, transport
scenarioEvents.description: Tube is secured, sedation is maintained, ventilation rate is controlled to keep EtCO2 in the target range, and the patient is transported to a trauma center capable of managing severe TBI.
relatedChecklist: Maintain post-intubation sedation; reassess RASS/comfort en route
Transport to highest level trauma center per GCS 3–13 criteria

scenarioEvents.name: RSI attempted without adequate preoxygenation
scenarioEvents.description: Crew skips the required two-minute preoxygenation period and proceeds directly to sedation and paralysis. SpO2 falls rapidly during the intubation attempt.
relatedChecklist: Abort attempt at SpO2 <90%; resume BVM with PEEP to reoxygenate

scenarioEvents.name: Hyperventilation drives EtCO2 low
scenarioEvents.description: Ventilation rate exceeds the protocol-directed target after intubation, driving EtCO2 below 30 mmHg and risking cerebral vasoconstriction that worsens secondary brain injury.
relatedChecklist: Reduce ventilation rate to 10/min; retarget EtCO2 to 35–45 mmHg
